Convincing solutions to all of these problems are required to reduce the uncertainty introduced by all factors affecting the sys- tem, including the ones proposed for the future. This reduction should lead to the minimization of differences in the initial con- ditions of the vision system improving its chaotic behaviour in the context of soft computing. chunks.text: obsta- cles we carried forward the work of obstacle detection in RHEA project [31]. Identifying dynamic obstacles, people walking into the crops area, is important for preventing and ensuring the safety of people/animals and also to guarantee the continuity of the pro- cess. Our proposal is based on image processing analysis supported by the combination of spectral segmentation and temporal dif- ferences. Firstly, obstacle detection is performed in the spatial scale and then, a temporal differencing is carried out for motion detection. This approach addresses the problem of uncertainty in uncontrolled outdoor agricultural and dynamical scenarios involv- ing agricultural machinery. Although the proposed approach could be considered deterministic in nature, the high variability in the illumination conditions, camera vibrations, unknown and unex- pected static or dynamic objects introduce the aforementioned uncertainty. Hence, the proposed computer vision approach deals with differences in initial conditions, belonging to a kind of systems with a chaotic deterministic behaviour in the context of applied soft computing in agricultural machinery. The experimental results show that our method is suitable and effective in the context of our agricultural scenarios. We also show that trees detection is possible from the point of view of image analysing processing, making it a useful contribution for path localization and path mapping tasks. More speciﬁcally, another important contribution is that no training process is required. It is entirely based on a combination of digital and image analysis techniques. Object detection on video sequences is still an open issue demanding special attention in view of the commercialization of these vehicles in the future. We have established an important basis 96 Y. Campos et al. / Applied Soft Computing 45 (2016) 86–97 for continuing towards ﬁnding a global solution to the problem of detecting obstacles for safe navigation in autonomous agricul- tural vehicles. ## Análise da Pesquisa

**1. Área Computacional:**

Visão Computacional Clássica (o método é baseado em processamento de imagem, segmentação espectral e diferenças temporais, sem menção a aprendizado de máquina ou redes neurais).

**2. Sensores Utilizados:**

Câmera RGB (CCD-based high-resolution camera operating in the visible RGB spectral range).

**3. Bibliotecas, Frameworks ou Arquiteturas:**

Não informado no contexto.

**4. Solução / Tarefa Principal:**

Detecção de obstáculos (objetos/obstáculos em vídeos agrícolas para garantir a segurança da navegação autônoma de veículos agrícolas). A tarefa inclui também análise de movimento dos obstáculos e detecção de árvores para auxílio em tarefas de localização e mapeamento.
